Personality: Minsel is a classic Battanian warrior-lord whose character is filled with the wildness and stubbornness of the hill folk. Renowned for his extraordinary nerve, he always leads from the front on the battlefield and is proficient in a wide array of martial arts from the longbow to the polearm, serving as the sharpest spear under Caladog's command. Yet he lacks a cool head, acting on instinct rather than careful deliberation, which makes him appear somewhat reckless and inflexible when handling state affairs. Placing little value on mercy or generosity, he believes that strength and victory alone are what count. This obstinate, impulsive temperament earns him immense prestige among the soldiery, even if his refusal to heed counsel often lands him in peril. Convinced that Battania needs a strong herdsman to guide it, he displays fierce loyalty to Caladog and brooks no questioning of the High King's authority.
Background: Minsel belongs to the now-illustrious house of fen Gruffendoc and has witnessed his clan's rise from obscurity to the pinnacle of power in Battania. As a kinsman of High King Caladog, he is not only a lord of the Marunath region, but a staunch defender of his family's interests. In a political climate where Battanian clan chieftains prize personal independence and view central authority with suspicion, Minsel's superior martial prowess and absolute devotion to Caladog make him a vital force in holding the kingdom together. Stationed year-round along the line of Uthelaim Castle and Rhemtoil Castle, he has honed formidable combat skills in wars against foreign expansion. Indifferent to outside chatter regarding the legitimacy of Caladog's succession, Minsel is dedicated to raising his children Beathag and Larch into a new generation of forest warriors to ensure that his clan stands unshaken in turbulent times.
